template.name: Jira Epic, User Story and Bug Templates

execution_model.description: Each query is intended for similarity retrieval against the active knowledge base. Queries use source document terminology and source identifiers. Internal Jira IDs are generated outside the LLM.

global_rules: Use only the source documents in the active knowledge base as authority for project facts.
The Jira template provides output structure and guidance only; placeholders and examples are not project facts.
Keep each retrieval question focused on one information need.
Prefer the exact vocabulary and section terminology used in the source document.
Do not invent project facts, actors, benefits, priorities, releases, story points, assignees, labels, components, dependencies, risks, assumptions, rules, metrics, or relationships.
Preserve source IDs, wording, dates, numbers, priorities, conditions, and measurable details.
Use null for unsupported scalar values and [] where an array has no supported items.
Every source reference must support the specific returned value.
Never ask the LLM to generate internal Jira Story IDs or Jira Epic keys.
Use source requirement IDs such as FR-001 as the stable story join key; the assembler creates US-FR-001.

queries.question: What is the name of the main business capability, solution area, or initiative described in the source?
rules: Prefer a capability or solution name explicitly stated in the source.
Do not use a business objective ID as the Epic Name.
Do not copy a template example value.

queries.question: What is the summary of this initiative or solution?
rules: Prefer the business background, project purpose, problem statement, and future-state description.
Return a concise source-grounded summary.

queries.question: What business objectives is this initiative trying to achieve?
rules: Use the Business Objectives section.
Preserve objective IDs and wording.

queries.question: What business problem is this initiative trying to solve, or what opportunity is identified?
rules: Prefer the Business Problem Statement and Business Background.
Do not turn future-state requirements into the problem statement.

queries.question: What business benefit or expected outcome is described for this initiative?
rules: Use explicitly described benefits or outcomes.
Do not invent a benefit.

queries.question: What capabilities, processes, or activities are explicitly in scope?
rules: Use the explicit In Scope section.
Return each scope item separately.

queries.question: What capabilities, processes, or activities are explicitly out of scope?
rules: Use the explicit Out of Scope section.
Do not classify constraints or risks as out of scope unless the source does.

queries.question: What solution, future-state capability, or business process is described for this initiative?
rules: Prefer the Future-State Business Requirements section.
Do not introduce technical implementation details.

queries.question: Who are the stakeholders, user roles, or personas identified in the source, and what responsibility or interest is stated for each?
rules: Prefer the Stakeholders section.
Do not infer requirement-level relationships.

queries.question: What success measures, KPIs, targets, or measurable outcomes are stated?
rules: Prefer the Business Objectives section.
Preserve numerical targets exactly.

queries.question: What dependencies are explicitly stated for this initiative?
rules: Return only statements explicitly identified as dependencies.

queries.question: What risks are explicitly stated for this initiative?
rules: Return only statements explicitly identified as risks.

queries.question: What assumptions are explicitly stated for this initiative?
rules: Use the explicit Assumptions section.
Return only explicit assumptions.

queries.question: What priority is explicitly stated for this initiative or Epic?
rules: Do not infer Epic priority from individual FR priorities.

queries.question: What target release or fix version is explicitly stated for this initiative?
rules: Return null when no release or fix version is stated.

queries.question: What labels or components are explicitly stated for this initiative?
rules: Return null when none are explicitly stated.
Do not invent Jira labels or components.

queries.question: What source document sections, requirement IDs, or other references support the Epic information?
rules: Return only references present in the source.

queries.question: What acceptance criteria are explicitly stated for the capabilities represented by this Epic?
rules: Use the dedicated Acceptance Criteria section.
Preserve AC IDs and Given/When/Then meaning.
Do not invent Epic acceptance criteria.

queries.question: What functional requirements are listed in the Functional Requirements section?
rules: Return one item for each functional requirement ID.
Use the FR ID exactly as source_requirement_id, such as FR-001.
Keep story_title and capability close to the requirement wording.
Do not generate a Jira Story ID.

queries.question: Which user role or actor is explicitly associated with each functional requirement?
rules: Use the Functional Requirements and Current Process sections first.
Use Stakeholders or Acceptance Criteria only when they explicitly identify the actor for the FR.
Use the FR ID as source_requirement_id.

queries.question: What does each functional requirement say the system shall allow, support, provide, or do?
rules: Use the Functional Requirements wording as the story description.
Return a business objective only when an explicit mapping is stated.
Use the FR ID as source_requirement_id.

queries.question: What priority is listed for each functional requirement?
rules: Read the Priority value from the Functional Requirements section.
Do not infer priority.
Use the FR ID as source_requirement_id.

queries.question: What story points are explicitly stated for each functional requirement?
rules: Return null when story points are not stated.
Do not estimate story points.

queries.question: What sprint, release, or fix version is explicitly stated for each functional requirement?
rules: Return null when not explicitly stated.
Do not invent a sprint or release.

queries.question: What components or labels are explicitly stated for each functional requirement?
rules: Return null when not explicitly stated.
Do not invent Jira labels or components.

queries.question: Who is explicitly assigned to each functional requirement or story?
rules: Return null when no assignee is stated.
Do not infer an assignee from the persona.

queries.question: What dependency is explicitly associated with each functional requirement?
rules: Return only explicit story-level dependencies.
Do not copy the entire project dependency list to every story.

queries.question: What UX, API, attachment, or supporting artefact reference is explicitly mentioned for each functional requirement?
rules: Return only explicit references.
Do not invent design or API artefacts.

queries.question: What unresolved clarification, ambiguity, or missing requirement detail is explicitly identified for each functional requirement?
rules: Return only explicit unresolved issues.
Do not turn missing Jira planning fields into clarification issues.

queries.question: What must be true before each functional requirement can be performed or the process can proceed?
rules: Search the functional requirement, current/future process, business rules, and acceptance criteria for explicit conditions.
Do not invent technical preconditions.

queries.question: What normal process steps are described for each functional requirement?
rules: Use the Current Process and Future-State Business Requirements sections.
Tie the returned steps to the FR.
Do not invent implementation steps.

queries.question: What alternative process path is explicitly described for each functional requirement?
rules: Return null when no explicit alternative path is described.
Do not invent an alternative path.

queries.question: What exception, failure, hold, rejection, or error behavior is explicitly described for each functional requirement?
rules: Use Business Rules, Future-State Business Requirements, and Acceptance Criteria.
Do not invent generic technical failures.

queries.question: Which business rule applies to each functional requirement, and what does the rule say?
rules: Use the Business Rules section and explicit FR mappings.
Return the rule only when its applicability to the FR is supported.
Do not classify NFRs or constraints as business rules.

queries.question: What data, fields, documents, or information are explicitly required by each functional requirement?
rules: Use explicit data items from Functional Requirements and related source sections.
Do not infer fields from a requirement title.

queries.question: What security, privacy, access-control, audit, or compliance requirement explicitly applies to each functional requirement?
rules: Use only clearly applicable source requirements.
Do not copy every global security requirement to every story.
Do not add generic best practices.

queries.question: What non-functional requirement explicitly applies to each functional requirement?
rules: Use the NFR section and any explicit applicability evidence.
Do not attach unrelated NFRs to every story.

queries.question: What unresolved business question or missing information is explicitly identified for each functional requirement?
rules: Return only explicitly unresolved questions or missing information.
Do not invent questions because a template field is empty.

queries.question: What acceptance criterion is mapped to each functional requirement, and what are its Given, When, and Then conditions?
rules: Use the dedicated Acceptance Criteria section.
Use the Mapped Requirement value to associate the AC with the FR.
Preserve AC IDs and Given/When/Then wording.
Do not invent acceptance criteria.

queries.question: Does the source describe an actual defect, failed behavior, or actual-versus-expected discrepancy that could be recorded as a Jira bug?
rules: Create a bug candidate only when an actual/current defect or discrepancy is explicitly documented.
Do not convert future-state requirements into bugs.
Do not use template examples as evidence.
Return [] when the source documents expected behavior but no actual defect.
Incident details that are absent from the source must remain null.

queries.question: What relationships are explicitly shown in the source traceability matrix between business objectives, business requirements, functional requirements, and acceptance criteria?
rules: Use the Traceability Matrix as the primary source.
Preserve the source IDs and mappings.
Do not invent Jira IDs.
